sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: The Muslim League withdrew its acceptance of the **Cabinet Mission Plan** in July 1946 after Nehru's press conference regarding the grouping of provinces.
• **The Call**: Jinnah declared August 16, 1946, as 'Direct Action Day' to achieve Pakistan by 'direct means'.
• **The Epicenter**: Calcutta (Kolkata) became the primary site of violence, leading to the **Great Calcutta Killings**.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The failure of the British administration to maintain law and order during the transition of power, leading to widespread communal polarization.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Pressure on British to concede Pakistan
Mains: Analysis of League's political strategy

items.definition: The failed attempt to keep India united through a three-tier administrative structure; its rejection triggered the Direct Action Day.
The massive communal violence that erupted on August 16, 1946, lasting several days, resulting in thousands of deaths and mass displacement.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Political Strategy**: Use of 'Direct Action' as a tool for constitutional bargaining.
• **Administrative Failure**: The inability of the H.S. Suhrawardy-led Bengal government to contain the violence.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Communalization of the police and civil services.
• **Solutions**: The eventual realization that partition was inevitable to prevent total anarchy.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'C-D-A' (Cabinet-Direct-Action).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Cabinet Mission (May 1946) -> Direct Action Day (August 1946) -> Interim Government (September 1946).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the date of Direct Action Day (August 16) with the formation of the Interim Government (September 2). Ensure the sequence is clear.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Communal Veto' to describe the League's strategy during the 1946 negotiations.

keyTakeaways: Direct Action Day was a direct consequence of the breakdown of the Cabinet Mission Plan.
It signaled the shift from constitutional agitation to communal violence as a political tool.
The event made the partition of India almost unavoidable in the eyes of the British and the Congress.
